source.document: Cessna Model 172 Series 1977 thru 1986 Service Manual D2065-3-13, Revision 3 (1995), Copyright Cessna Aircraft Company
source.note: Facts transcribed from the manual with page references only; no page images are reproduced.

meta.page_refs: pdf = 1-based PDF page; manual = printed page label (e.g. '20-49'). Section 20 diagrams are scanned drawings (no text layer) read visually from 300-500 dpi renders.
meta.system: 28-volt DC, single-wire negative-ground; 24-volt battery (beginning with 1978 models). 60 A alternator with alternator control unit (ACU) and low-voltage warning. Split primary bus + avionics bus via 40 A avionics power switch-breaker. (16-3, pdf 410; 20-47, pdf 588)
meta.wire_numbering: Wire numbers are pre-1990s Cessna circuit codes: function letters + sequence (e.g. 'PA23' = D.C. power / battery circuit wire 23); gauge is a separate column in each drawing's wire table. Code letters on 20-2/20-3 (pdf 543-544).

effectivity_rules.interpretation: 'SER (SR9624) & ON' = applies to 172P; 'THRU SER (SRxxxx)' = effective up to that serial break (superseded at it). Flag notes 'APPLIES TO R172 & FR172 ONLY' excluded. SR9944 appears on drawings but is not in the SR cross-reference table (it bounds only R172 wires and LB7).
effectivity_rules.voltage: All 12-volt diagrams (20-4..20-38, pdf 545-579, drawing 0570101) are INACTIVE thru SR8453/SR8454 (1978) and do not apply. Only drawing 0570311 (24-volt, pdf 580-639) pages applicable to 17274010+ are used.

as_drawn: [pdf 590 / 20-49] 172P (SR9624 & on): battery (item 8, C614002-0101) negative to ground via battery ground (item 5, 0412007); positive via PA26 (4 ga) to battery contactor (item 9, S-2475-1) main terminal. A 22 GA JUMPER on that battery-side terminal feeds the contactor coil/diode top terminal; diode assy (item 4, 0770728) is across the coil. Coil other terminal -> PA29 (22 ga) -> master switch BAT half (item 6, S-1994-1-1); master switch BAT half other terminal -> PA11 (22 ga) -> ground. Contactor output terminal -> PA23 (4 ga) -> starter contactor (item 2, S-2443-1); starter contactor output -> KA12 (4 ga) -> starter. Starter contactor coil is fed from ignition switch (see 20-55).

as_drawn: [pdf 587 / 20-46, 20-47, 20-48] Primary bus bar (item 8, 0570451) is fed from the ammeter via DA6 at the TURN COORD end terminal (see 20-50). Breakers on primary bus (main view, later 172P): AIR COND/CIR FAN 5,10 (optional, HE2), ALT 60 (PB34 to alternator), ALT FIELD 5 (PB1 to master ALT/ACU), FLAP 10 (CC1), PITOT HEAT (FB1), INST 5 (KA1 mag sw, EB18 fuel gauges, EE8 oil temp, PB14 ACU low-volt lamp), INT LT 5 (WE1 vacuum-out lt, LA8 dome lt sw, LB1 dimmer, LA1 aux inst lt), NAV LT 5 (LD14), BCN LT 10 (LF1), LAND LT 20 (LC12 to ldg & taxi lt sw), STROBE LT 5 (LD15 to strobe sw), TURN COORD 5 (FA1). PA32 (10 ga) runs from the bus feed terminal to the 40 A avionics master switch-breaker CM3589-40; PA8 (10 ga) from it to the avionics bus (item 6, 0570419) carrying RADIO 1-5 positions (no ratings printed) and AUTO PILOT 5. Early 172P alternates: LANDING LT 15 A feeding taxi LE1 and ldg LC1 directly (SR9624-SR10034); HC4 cigar lighter feed tied to the bus feed terminal (SR9624-SR10056).

components.name: Electrical system (overall)
components.description: 28-volt DC, single wire, negative ground; 24-volt battery (beginning with 1978 models). Thru 1977: 14-volt system, 12-volt battery.
components.effectivity: 172P: 28V system / 24V battery

components.name: Battery
components.location: mounted on the forward left hand side of the firewall
components.description: 24-volt, approx 12.75 ampere-hour standard; optional approx 15.5 ampere-hour (beginning with 17269742 and F17201730). Normal battery reads 23 V or more on 28 V system under load.
components.effectivity: Beginning 17269742 (covers 172P). Alternates: thru 17269309 12V ~25 Ah; 17269310-17269605 24V ~17 Ah

components.name: Battery pan / battery installation (pan, cover, bolt, terminal cover, sta-strap, elbow, drain tube, clamp, ground strap)
components.location: forward side of firewall, left (pan-mounted; battery box riveted to firewall thru 17272884)
components.description: Beginning with 1980 models battery sits in pan (item 20) with cover (3) and long bolts (2); drain tube (9) via elbow (8); ground strap (21) from negative terminal; positive terminal under terminal cover (4) secured by sta-strap.
components.effectivity: Sheet 5 beginning 17274010 & F17202070; sheet 7 beginning 17275340 & F17202170 adds shield (39), cooling duct (40), clamps (41)

components.name: Battery box (alternate)
components.location: riveted to the forward side of the firewall; vent tube protrudes through bottom of aircraft
components.description: Acid-proof painted box; acid proof lacquer CES1054-381 for repairs.
components.effectivity: THRU 17272884 AND F17201909 only - not 172P

components.name: Battery contactor
components.location: on the firewall (beginning with 1978 models); bolted to side of battery box thru 1977
components.description: Plunger type, actuated by master switch (battery side). Coil resistance 50-70 ohms on 28 V aircraft (BAT terminal to master-switch terminal). Silicon diode across contactor: large diode terminal to BAT terminal of contactor; small diode terminal and master switch wire to minus terminal of contactor coil. Nylon cover over terminals. Smallest terminal = master switch terminal.
components.effectivity: 172P; 1981+ removal procedure p426

components.name: Battery contactor diode (spike suppression)
components.location: across battery contactor terminals
components.description: Silicon diode eliminates spiking of transistorized radio equipment.

components.name: Battery contactor closing circuit: 5 amp fuse, resistor and diode
components.location: on the firewall fuse bracket adjacent to the battery
components.description: Shunts a small charge around the battery contactor so ground power may close the contactor when the battery is too dead to energize it.
components.figure: Figure 16-2 sheet 5 items 26 (Clock Fuse), 27 (Fuse Battery Contactor Closing Circuit), 28 (Diode)
components.effectivity: Sheet 5 beginning 17274010

components.name: Clock fuse
components.location: firewall fuse bracket adjacent to battery (Fig 16-2 sheet 5 item 26)
components.effectivity: beginning 17274010

components.name: Starter contactor
components.location: firewall, grouped with battery contactor and ground service contactor (Fig 16-2 sheets 4-7)
components.description: Cover (Starter Contactor) item 25; wires: to battery contactor, to starter, to ignition switch, ground wire.

components.name: Ground service (external power) contactor
components.location: firewall, grouped with battery and starter contactors
components.description: Reverse-polarity protection: silicon junction diode in series with coil so contactor will not close with reversed ground power. Coil 50-70 ohms on 24 volt system (small coil terminal to ground).
components.effectivity: Optional equipment

components.name: Ground service receptacle
components.location: beneath battery pan on bracket assembly, accessed through door in cowl skin (Fig 16-3 / 16-2 sheet 5 item 29)
components.description: Optional; diode board at rear of receptacle; ground strap on negative stud of receptacle. Avionics master must be OFF when external power applied; close master switch before removing ground power plug when starting.
components.figure: Figure 16-3 sheet 2 (BEGINNING WITH 1981 MODELS); Figure 16-2 sheets 5,7
components.effectivity: 1981+ sheet 2; thru 1980 sheet 1

components.name: Ground service diode board
components.location: at rear of ground service receptacle
components.description: Check polarity/continuity; replace diode board assembly if open/mis-wired.

components.name: Master switch
components.location: instrument panel (not further located in Sec 16)
components.description: Interlocking split rocker: battery mode (BAT) right-hand side, alternator mode (ALT) left-hand side. Alternator cannot be on line without battery.

components.name: Split bus bar (primary bus + avionics bus bar)
components.location: behind instrument panel at circuit breaker row
components.description: Electrical (primary) side fed from battery contactor via ammeter; electronic side fed through avionics master switch (beginning 1978).
components.figure: Figure 16-1 sheets 2,3 (items 9 Avionics Bus Bar, 10 Primary Bus)
components.effectivity: Sheet 2: 1981 THRU 1982 MODELS; Sheet 3: BEGINNING WITH 1983 MODELS

components.name: Avionics master switch
components.location: instrument panel breaker row, right end, wired between primary bus and avionics bus bar (Fig 16-1 item 8)
components.description: Must be OFF when external power is applied. Replaced split-bus relay of thru-1977 models.
components.effectivity: beginning 1978 models

components.name: Ammeter
components.location: instrument panel
components.description: Connected between battery and aircraft bus; indicates current to/from battery. Fig 16-1 sheets 2-3 show wire 'TO AMMETER' attached at primary bus near TURN COORD breaker.

components.name: Alternator
components.location: engine, belt driven (Fig 16-4)
components.description: 60-ampere, three phase, delta connected, integral silicon diode rectifiers; 28 volts at 60 amperes (beginning 1978). Field ('F' terminal to case) 12-20 ohms. Belt tension: used belt slips at 7-9 ft-lb, new belt 11-13 ft-lb.
components.effectivity: Mounting bracket detail B: '* BEGINNING WITH 17273934 AND F17202040' (vs 'THRU 17273938' for alternate - overlapping serials as printed)

components.name: Alternator control unit (ACU)
components.location: mounted on the left hand side of the firewall
components.description: Solid state voltage regulator with over-voltage and low-voltage sensors; not adjustable. Pin 1 (Blue wire) to alternator F terminal; Pin 3 (Red wire) to master switch to bus bar; Pin 2 (Orange wire) to alternator BAT terminal. Bus voltage with alternator on 28.4-28.9 V (1979+ troubleshooting). Housing plug/cap connector; ground wire; terminal block.
components.effectivity: Beginning 1979 models. Sheet 4: '17276885 THRU 17276199' (as printed; probably 17272885) & F17201910-F17202233, washers (11) beginning with 1981 models; Sheet 5: BEGINNING WITH 17276200 AND F17202234 (spacer 11)

components.name: Low-voltage warning light (red, 'LOW VOLTAGE')
components.location: instrument panel
components.description: Low-voltage sensor in ACU turns light on below 24.5 volts. Filament test: ALT half of master off, BAT on.
components.effectivity: Beginning 1979 models (thru 1978: 'HIGH VOLTAGE' light + separate over-voltage sensor)

components.name: Over-voltage sensor (separate, alternate)
components.location: mounting bracket just forward of instrument panel on left side (1978); on wire bundle behind panel thru 1977
components.effectivity: Not 172P

components.name: Terminal block (alternator/ACU)
components.location: firewall, adjacent to ACU (Fig 16-5 item 3, with cover item 10)
components.description: Joins wire to alternator (1) and wire to alternator circuit breaker (2).
components.effectivity: Beginning 17271453 and F17201795

components.name: Circuit breakers (panel)

components.description: Labels per Fig 16-1; ratings not printed in Section 16 figures except landing/taxi 20 amp (text) and cigar lighter thermal breaker.

components.figure: Figure 16-6 sheet 3 (Detail B BEGINNING WITH 17275035 AND F17202135)
components.effectivity: BEGINNING WITH 17275035 AND F17202135 (1982-86). Which wing is not stated in text.

components.name: Navigation lights

components.description: Rocker switch on instrument panel; circuit breaker on panel. Receptacle/electrical leads in wing tip (Fig 16-7 detail A).

components.location: white strobe on each wing tip with nav lights; individual power supplies mounted on each wing tip rib
components.description: Capacitor discharge xenon tube; 24 volts at power supply red lead (beginning 1978). Power supply ground wire must not contact wing structure. High voltage: wait 5 min.
components.effectivity: 172P uses 17268212+ detail

components.name: Flashing beacon light
components.location: attached to the vertical fin tip
components.description: Iodine-vapor lamp switched by solid-state flasher; approx 45 flashes per minute. Lamp filament perpendicular to longitudinal axis (Detail C beginning 17273742 & F17202000).

components.name: Beacon flasher assembly

components.effectivity: Spacer (17) THRU 17272894; Z Bracket (18) BEGINNING WITH 17272895

harness_routing.description: Battery-area cabling: positive cable from battery to battery contactor; wires from contactors run under the contactor covers, secured with sta-straps; wire bundle (items 14 to ammeter, 18 to receptacle, 15 to ignition switch, 16 to starter) leaves contactor group toward firewall

Contactor terminal wiring (Detail B): ground service contactor - wire 30 (to starter contactor), 31 (to ground service), 17 (to diode board), 32 ground; starter contactor - 33 (to battery contactor) and 30 on input stud, 16 (to starter) on output stud, 32 ground, small terminal lead; battery contactor - 12 (diode leads), 35 (to starter contactor), 36 (to clock fuse), 37 jumper wire, 38 (to battery)

harness_routing.description: Battery drain tube and (1983+) cooling duct routed down from battery pan below cowl; shield over battery
Ground service receptacle cable (to contactor) from receptacle studs, through bracket assembly below battery pan; diode board and ground strap on receptacle studs

ACU wiring: wire bundle with housing plug/cap secured by sta-straps; wire to alternator and wire to alternator circuit breaker joined at terminal block; alternator ground and ACU ground wire at ACU mounting bolt
Over-voltage sensor attached to the wire bundle behind instrument panel (thru 1977) / bracket forward of panel LH (1978)
Strobe power supply in each wing tip on wing tip rib; red power lead from aircraft supply to power supply; electrical leads to flash tube in nav light assembly

Control wheel map light cable runs inside control wheel tube from map light/rheostat to terminal board with fuse on back of stationary panel
Door post map light wires routed down front doorpost behind front doorpost shield to quick-disconnects; switch on shield
Pitot heater electrical leads exit top of pitot mast into wing
ELT coaxial cable from transmitter forward connector to antenna base on tailcone top; cable sta-strapped
